title: Pivot tables: months, % of total, and helper columns
explanation: Pivot tables can do more than add things up. They can group dates into months, show each group as a **share** of the total, and spread a second field across the top. And when the number you need isn't in the data, like profit, you add a **helper column** first, then pivot it.

tasks.prompt: Make a pivot of total gross by month, using the release dates. Click any cell inside the data, open the **Insert** tab at the top of the toolbar, and click **Pivot table**. The Insights panel opens on the right. Set Rows to Release date, Values to Gross ($M), Summarize by to Sum, and tick **Group dates by month**.
tasks.teach: Each movie has its own release date, so a pivot by date would have 18 rows. **Group dates by month** rolls them up into one row per month, which shows the trend.
hints: After setting Rows to Release date, the Group dates by month box becomes clickable.
Rows: Release date, Values: Gross ($M), Sum, and tick Group dates by month.
tasks.answer: Rows: Release date, Values: Gross ($M), Sum, Group dates by month ticked

tasks.prompt: Which month made the most money? Type its 3-letter name (like Jan) into K2.
hints: Look for the biggest monthly total.

tasks.prompt: Show each genre's share of all gross: Rows to Genre, Values to Gross ($M), Sum, untick Group dates by month, and tick **Show as % of total**.
tasks.teach: **Show as % of total** turns each number into a share of the Grand Total. The shares add up to 100%.
hints: Change Rows to Genre, then tick Show as % of total.
tasks.answer: Rows: Genre, Values: Gross ($M), Sum, Show as % of total ticked

tasks.prompt: Type Action's share into K3 as a decimal, rounded to 2 places (for example, 25% is 0.25).
hints: Read Action's % from the pivot, then divide by 100 and round to 2 decimals.

tasks.prompt: Profit isn't in the data, so make a helper column. In H2, work out profit: gross − budget. Then copy it down to H19.
tasks.teach: A **helper column** is a formula column you add so a pivot can use it. Real Excel also has "calculated fields" inside pivots, but analysts usually prefer helper columns, because you can see and check every number.
hints: Then copy it down to H19.
tasks.answer: =F2-G2 in H2, then copy down to H19

tasks.prompt: Pivot the new column: Rows to Genre, Values to Profit ($M), Sum, and untick Show as % of total. If Profit doesn't appear in the Values list, click **Use selected cells** at the top of the panel to re-read the data.
hints: Click a cell in the data, then Use selected cells, so the panel sees column H.

tasks.prompt: Last one: which genre made the most profit? Type it into K4.
hints: Look for the biggest profit total.
Horror, with 158: small budgets, solid gross.

recap: Group dates by month rolls daily dates into months, and Show as % of total turns numbers into shares. When a number isn't in the data, add a helper column, then pivot it.
